items.summary: NVIDIA's open-source AICR now includes a qualified AI bill of materials component from Google's k8s-aibom, adding workload discovery on top of its validated configuration generation for GPU-accelerated Kubernetes. The pairing covers the gap between deployment intent and observed workloads; upstream measured controller inventory overhead at about four API-server requests per minute over 15 minutes, with average CPU usage of 2.2 millicores and a memory working set of 28 to 34 MiB.
items.title: NVIDIA Adds Runtime AI Inventory to Its GPU Platform Tooling

items.summary: Google introduced the Gemini Decisions API, powered by a new model (gemini-decision-1), offering fast closed-set decisions across text, images, audio, video and PDFs. It scores options in one pass with 150-250 ms latency at $0.10 per 1M input tokens and zero output-token billing, reportedly nearly 5x cheaper than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite.
items.title: Google Unveils Gemini Decisions API for Fast Multimodal Choices

items.summary: Taiwan's TSMC plans to invest up to $500 million each in OpenAI preferred stock reserved for large investors and Anthropic common shares at its expected IPO price, per Reuters. The deal would give the chipmaker stakes in leading AI developers even as it profits from AI data center buildout.
items.title: TSMC Plans $1 Billion Investment in Anthropic and OpenAI

items.summary: A blog post dated 11th November 2026 introduces aws-emulator, an official emulator from AWS that lets testers run against a local clone of the company's services without provisioning a paid API key. The tool is written in Rust by what the author calls 'a huge swarm of agents,' recording 29,684 commits across the project's first three weeks. It currently requires Docker on macOS or Windows.
items.title: AWS Releases Official Rust Emulator for Local Service Testing

items.summary: Researchers at Google Research introduce an investigational machine learning framework that translates passive wearable signals into a coachable health age, simulates personalized 12-week habit trajectories with an action-conditioned world model, and expands to routine blood biomarkers to track cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) health. The team validated the approach across cohorts including roughly 100,000 Fitbit users and evaluated a multimodal CKM model in 819 participants. They note the models are investigational research prototypes rather than clinical diagnostic tools.
items.title: Google Research Introduces Wearable-Based Health Age Framework for CKM Risk Profiling and Personalized Coaching

items.summary: Bloomberg reports Congress is preparing to subpoena Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over his relationship with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive and suspected Chinese spy. House Republicans Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford sent him a letter requesting a closed-door briefing. Committee Chairman Moolenaar said Huang must respond by end of Wednesday or he will likely be subpoenaed; Mast’s committee is preparing one too. Nvidia did not immediately comment.
items.title: Congress Prepares Subpoena for Nvidia CEO Over Alleged Chinese Spy Affair

items.summary: Google has launched the Gemini Decisions API powered by a new model, Gemini Decision 1 (gemini-decision-1), which scores up to 1,000 typed questions against one shared input and returns calibrated probabilities. It targets branching calls inside agents such as routing, policy checks, tool selection and grading, billing at $0.10 per 1M input tokens with zero output tokens billed. Google reports it leads 7 of 9 accuracy benchmarks in its table, including 92.2% on JevBench (public split), while trailing TypeSafe Jev 1.14 on When2Call (79.9% vs 82.0%). All figures are self-reported by Google; refusals and safety blocks count as incorrect.
items.title: Google Launches Decision-Scoring Model for AI Agents

items.summary: ZDNET reports Google announced two free features for Fi Wireless customers on Pixel 9 or newer, Samsung phones with One UI 9+, and select Motorola models. The mobile feature automatically switches between the fastest available networks if a connection slows; it runs on MEP technology and requires non-Fi SIMs disabled. Wi-Fi Auto Connect+ links to faster connections in millions of locations without login. Google says both work internationally on Unlimited Premium and Flexible plans.
items.title: Google Fi Auto-Switches Between Networks and Wi-Fi

items.summary: Google DeepMind released AlphaGenome 2, a DNA model that predicts variant effects in specific cell types. Unlike its predecessor, which averaged across bulk tissues, the new conditional sequence-to-function model resolves closely related cell types and adapts to unseen single-cell datasets without fine-tuning. Training used 2048 TPU v4 chips; weights are available upon final publication. On TenK10K single-cell eQTLs across 28 immune cell types, AlphaGenome 2 recovered 30% of causal variants at 90% precision versus 16% for fine-tuned AlphaGenome 1. A precomputed atlas scores about 7 million common and GWAS variants across 510 conditions. Access is API-only and non-commercial for now.
items.title: Google DeepMind Releases AlphaGenome 2 for Cell-Type-Specific Variant Effects

items.summary: Databricks opened its new headquarters at One Sansome Street in San Francisco last week, a 235,000+ square foot space. The company says it is investing over $1 billion into San Francisco operations by early 2028, and hosting its Data + AI Summit there through 2030, expected to generate nearly $1 billion for the city. Databricks now has over 12,000 employees worldwide.
items.title: Databricks Opens New San Francisco Headquarters and Commits $1 Billion Investment

items.summary: Databricks is introducing the new Genie, an autonomous AI coworker that proactively handles long-running enterprise work within guardrails set by users. The product combines Genie Ontology for trusted business context, Genie Search for hybrid information retrieval across lakehouse and connected systems, Unity Gateway to control tool access and spending, and Genie Agents for specialized team expertise. Databricks states thousands of teams already use these tools in marketing, sales, finance, and operations. In a benchmark built with Turing, Genie Ontology answered correctly in 91% of task runs, 1.6 times the rate of a stronger frontier agent while using less than half as many tokens. A customer from S&P Global Energy says productizing knowledge that once took a full development cycle now takes days.
items.title: Databricks Unveils Autonomous AI Coworker Genie

items.summary: British startup Fractile raised a $720 million Series C backed by Britain's Sovereign AI Fund, aiming to strengthen the U.K.'s role in purpose-built AI chip hardware. The round was led by Thrive Capital and others at an estimated valuation over £5 billion. CEO Walter Goodwin said funding will help ship its first chips next year.
items.title: Fractile Raises $720M Series C for AI Chips

items.summary: Jared Sine of GoDaddy cautions that as AI agents increasingly navigate the internet, a few dominant platforms may become gatekeepers controlling customer access and visibility. He notes millions already rely on chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude, with Meta’s Muse potentially acting for users soon (s4). Citing Bain & Company, he says purchases initiated by AI could reach hundreds of billions in US e-commerce activity by 2030 (s17), risking closed ecosystems. Sine contrasts this with the open internet built on standards like DNS and calls for an open Agent Name Service to preserve competition over private permission slips (s26).
items.title: GoDaddy's Sine Warns AI Could Gatekeep Online Access

items.summary: Fintech firm Airwallex plans to invest more than $2 billion in Singapore over the next five years, expanding its local workforce beyond 1,000 employees. The company currently employs more than 750 people there and expects continued hiring focused on artificial intelligence, product development and engineering. Its first-half 2026 revenue growth reached 90% year-on-year as it grows payments and agentic business accounts for small and medium-sized enterprises.
items.title: Airwallex Commits Over $2 Billion and Expands Singapore Workforce

items.summary: Osman V.P. Mohamed of the Singapore Land Authority, National Heritage Board and Urban Redevelopment Authority proposes adapting historic Marsiling underground fuel storage facilities built in the early 1940s for wartime defence. He points to The Tank at the Art Gallery of New South Wales in Sydney as inspiration: a preserved World War II-era naval tank repurposed into an art gallery since 2022, with its concrete pillars and oil-stained walls kept intact. Mohamed argues Marsiling’s tunnels could become heritage or arts venues without demolition, possibly enabling Singapore-Australia cultural collaborations.
items.title: Singapore looks to Sydney for Marsiling tunnels reuse

items.summary: Shopee owner Sea missed analysts' earnings estimates as artificial intelligence costs climbed, sending its shares lower on Nov 10. Adjusted Ebitda rose 29% to US$931 million for the three months to September, below the estimated average of US$990 million, while revenue beat predictions at a 43% rise to US$8.6 billion. The stock fell 1.5%, weighed down by competition and AI spending plans.
items.title: Sea Misses Earnings Estimate Amid Rising AI Costs

items.summary: Will Knight introduced a virtual robot cat butler he trained with OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol to identify Bengal cats and eventually dispense treats, noting the vision system is not yet product-ready. He said simulating such behavior took only 'a few hours,' which he called incredible compared to weeks previously. Citing Ken Goldberg of UC Berkeley and Jim Fan of Nvidia, Knight described how AI models now automate detailed robot simulations and training. Fan noted that robots still have work to do before matching humans.
items.title: Robotics Developer Tests AI-Trained Virtual Cat Butler at CoRL

items.summary: Simon Willison updated his tools site with tag clouds for browsing JavaScript APIs, libraries and web API hosts used by each tool in his collection of 244 vibe-coded tools. He had leftover Fable 5.2 credits that he spent using tree-sitter to analyze the code. Recent posts include entries from November 9th and 3rd, plus one dated 2nd November.
items.title: Simon Willison Adds Tag Clouds to Tools Site

items.summary: Elon Musk announced Tesla will keep building the Cybertruck through summer 2027, five days after first saying it would end production around mid-2026. The extension follows growing fan pushback over slowing sales at about 10% of plan and a backlog built by Tesla itself. On the same day, prices rose up to 10%, with the cheapest model now $92,490 from $69,990 in early August.
items.title: Tesla Extends Cybertruck Production Amid Fan Backlash and Sales Concerns

items.summary: Tesla confirmed its first deliveries of Tesla Semis to Chicago, with the official @tesla_semi account posting that “Chicago’s first 50 Semis” are en route. The recipient is HMD Trucking, a family-owned carrier founded in 1998 running more than 650 trucks, which ordered 50 units after Tesla launched volume production at its Nevada factory on September 24 and claims it can build 50,000 a year. Owner Henry Malukas said the deal is worth about $15 million, roughly $300,000 per truck. The batch represents only 0.1% of full-year capacity; Tesla does not report Semi output or ramp schedules, so analysts treat “built for 50,000” as a ceiling rather than current production.
items.title: Tesla Confirms First Chicago Semi Delivery as Ramp Remains Uncertain

items.summary: North Carolina’s Department of Environmental Quality sent a scathing critique to Chemours, arguing the company’s cleanup proposal violates its 2019 consent order. DEQ Secretary Reid Wilson said “DEQ expects Chemours to clean up all the areas they have polluted” and that it will hold the company accountable no matter how long it takes. The agency cited missing data, flawed sampling methods and analyses across at least 10 counties. A spokesperson for Chemours said it can now move forward with studies in hand. Over $1.2 billion has been spent on partial compliance so far.
items.title: North Carolina Regulators Reject Chemours Cleanup Plan

items.summary: Ontario Power Generation said in a Tuesday earnings release that the first BWRX-300 unit at its Darlington site will not come online by its October 2030 target and will blow past its budget of $7.7 billion Canadian ($5.4 billion U.S.). The utility did not set new targets, working instead on a revised cost and schedule assessment expected to be substantially completed by mid-2027. This is the project's second slip after an original 2028 completion goal announced in late 2021.
items.title: Canada's first small modular reactor faces delays and cost overruns

items.summary: Reed notes Nvidia faces renewed risk if founder CEO Jensen Huang steps down or is implicated in investigations, as he made transformative bets like the 2006 CUDA platform and the $6.9 billion Mellanox acquisition that underpin AI computing. Even riding out turmoil may weaken Nvidia’s strategic vision against an ascending China with no data-center red tape.
items.title: Nvidia’s Future Depends on Jensen Huang Amid China Rise

items.summary: Indian School of Business professor Prasanna Tantri warns the Reserve Bank of India may struggle to meet its 4% inflation target as money supply and bank credit expand at their fastest combined pace in more than a decade. Citing data for October 31, currency in circulation rose 14.2%, cash with the public 14.7%, broad money grew from 16% to 16.5%, and commercial sector credit jumped 19.4%. No financial year since 2012–13 has seen such growth together. Tantri says meeting the target would require a sustained fall in money velocity, which he finds unlikely.
items.title: ISB Professor Warns RBI May Miss Inflation Target Amid Fast Money and Credit Growth

items.summary: Google announced it is adding its Gemini voice assistant, powered by the Gemini Live model, to Apple's CarPlay platform. The global rollout covers all Gemini users on iOS and every supported language. Users can start or resume conversations, interrupt Gemini while driving, and sync chats with their iPhone app so notes appear after parking.
items.title: Google Adds Gemini Voice AI to Apple CarPlay

items.summary: Bankers for Anthropic are considering whether to raise the lab’s IPO price, betting on strong demand that could lift its valuation to $1.5 trillion and fund more compute spending. The Information noted Big Tech firms Alphabet and Amazon may eventually hold 27% of the company. Rival OpenAI reportedly told investors revenue grew around 50% quarter-on-quarter to $10 billion.
items.title: Anthropic’s bankers weigh raising IPO valuation amid AI funding surge

items.summary: Jensen Huang built Nvidia into a multibillion-dollar AI chip company but never named a second-in-command, highlighting dependence on him. This week that reliance is being questioned after his board opened an independent investigation following his admission of an affair with Alice Huang, and President Donald Trump revealed the FBI is looking into it. Observers now ask who would run Nvidia if he had to go.
items.title: Nvidia's leadership vacuum tested by CEO scandal

items.summary: A study of active logging concessions across five Congo Basin countries finds that validating forest management plans reduces annual forest loss by nearly half, with benefits emerging only after several years. Using a difference-in-differences approach over 2000–2020 satellite data, the authors estimate validated concessions lose about 100 fewer hectares annually (±44), roughly 47% less than unvalidated ones. Before validation there is no significant effect; gains grow gradually and persist for up to 19 years.
items.title: Forest management plans gradually cut Congo Basin logging losses

items.summary: For the first time in months, U.S. gasoline averaged under $4 a gallon nationally, reaching $3.94 for regular, AAA reported Tuesday. De Haan of GasBuddy dismissed election theories; León of Rystad Energy cited falling Brent crude at about $90 a barrel and seasonal demand shifts as main drivers. Brito of Dow Jones Energy cautioned prices are still the highest ever this time of year.
items.title: Gasoline Prices Fall Below $4 as Crude Drops

items.summary: Australia's blue-chip companies are increasingly citing artificial intelligence as they cut jobs and move work offshore, unions and experts say. Qantas announced 850 job cuts tied to an Accenture-led overhaul raising accusations of 'AI washing.' Tech firms WiseTech, Atlassian and Telstra have also attributed losses to AI, while other firms expanded operations in India, the Philippines and Vietnam without mentioning it. Unions argue workers were replaced by lower-paid offshore staff rather than machines. The Reserve Bank noted AI had not yet caused widespread job losses amid a 4.7 per cent unemployment rate.
items.title: Australian Firms Face AI Washing Accusations Amid Job Cuts

items.summary: About a dozen Labour MPs voiced concerns about approving the Rosebank oil field off Shetland during a Westminster Hall debate, warning it is incompatible with UK climate commitments. Senior figures Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh declined to commit, citing affordability of energy bills as an overriding objective. Some backbenchers have organised a letter opposing approval, supported by more than 60 out of about 400 Labour MPs. The field hangs in the balance after a court ruled earlier approvals unlawful; Labour's 2024 manifesto pledged not to issue new licences for fields.
items.title: Labour MPs Oppose Rosebank Oil Field as Decision Nears

items.summary: Members of Parliament accuse the owner of Poundland, Gordon Brothers, of extracting millions from the retailer while it faced insolvency. The company seeks a two-week extension to secure a rescue deal and employs 12,000 people across 600 stores in the UK and Ireland. Committee chair Liam Byrne says he is “deeply concerned that Gordon Brothers’ behaviour may have jeopardised thousands of jobs on Britain’s high streets.” Poundland remains protected from creditors while bidders are sought.
items.title: MPs Blame Poundland Owner for Extracting Millions Amid Rescue Bid

items.summary: Poundland hopes emergency talks will extend a midnight deadline as it edges toward administration after owners Gordon Brothers restricted access to frozen cash. Sources close to the matter told the BBC that a release of £10m could postpone collapse while longer-term solutions are explored, though Williams said like-for-like sales rose 11.4% and profit reached £18.1m in the year to September.
items.title: Poundland Seeks Delay for Rescue Deal Amid Owner Dispute

items.summary: ITV plans to slash its programming budget after new figures showed UK film and high-end TV production spend fell more than £2bn over the last year. The broadcaster expects temporary savings of £30m, including £25m in content and £5m elsewhere, without staff cuts. ITV chief executive Carolyn McCall attributed weaker ad demand to macroeconomic uncertainty and increased digital advertising on global streaming platforms. Separately, British Film Institute figures showed UK film spending plunged by £2.08bn year on year as the industry faces a difficult 2026.
items.title: ITV Cuts Programming Budget Amid UK Production Spending Drop

items.summary: On Wednesday, United Airlines announced it would restrict access by artificial intelligence agents to its digital platforms over data security concerns. The move reflects divergent industry approaches as such tools grow capable of booking trips and performing tasks like flight check-in.
items.title: United Airlines Blocks AI Agents Over Security Concerns

items.summary: A report frames Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang as central to a Chinese spy scandal, alleging he had an extramarital affair with Singapore-based tech CEO Alice Huang and that state-of-the-art chips she purchased may have been smuggled back to mainland China. The New York Times reports US Secretary of State Marco Rubio raised the security concerns with Donald Trump.
items.title: Nvidia Co-Founder Jensen Huang at Center of China Spy Allegations

items.summary: SpaceX signed a €60 million deal with German company Singulus Technologies for solar cells, per a statement from founder Elon Musk. The order supports Starmind satellites planned for Texas in 2027. Singulus manufactures heterojunction solar cells and plans capacity of 100 gigawatts. SINGULUS executive Lars Lieberwirth said the partnership lets them industrialise capabilities at scale, while SpaceX's Mike Nicolls called it a durable option.
items.title: German Firm Signs €60 Million Solar Cell Deal With SpaceX

items.summary: New South Wales police launched a homicide investigation after a human torso was found in bushland on Sydney's lower north shore. Detectives and the state's homicide squad opened the inquiry, with forensic specialists seizing remains for examination while people were urged to contact police.
items.title: Sydney Police Launch Homicide Probe After Torso Found in Bushland

items.summary: Opponents of Israel's hardline prime minister are trying to remove him by building a new coalition, but may have to cross a red line drawn by most Israeli parties: work with Arab colleagues. The move is framed as necessary yet politically risky.
items.title: Israeli Rivals May Cross Red Line Over Arab Coalition Partners

items.summary: A driver arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence faces three murder counts after a Tuesday Los Angeles crash killed three people and critically injured two, police said. The incident occurred near North Hollywood metro station on Lankershim Boulevard. Authorities are reviewing video in what LA police chief Jim McDonnell called a “prolonged but very deliberate investigation.”
items.title: LA Driver Charged With DUI and Murder After Fatal Crash

items.summary: The Caine Prize for African Writing confirmed Simbarashe Kundizeza as the winner of this year's £10,000 ($13,000) award after an internal review found no evidence that his winning story was written with generative AI. Chair Ellah Wakatama said the investigation had been conducted carefully and fairly, including interviews and expert-led metadata analysis. The accusation followed a report by Vauhini Vara in The Atlantic.
items.title: Caine Prize confirms Zimbabwean writer after AI probe finds no evidence

items.summary: France's Alexia Barrier became the first woman to complete the Route du Rhum in the Ultim class, finishing fifth aboard IDEC Sport-CIC after a punishing transatlantic race. She crossed the line at 1542 local time (1942 GMT), completing the 3,542-nautical-mile course from Saint-Malo to Guadeloupe in 10 days, 7 hours and 40 minutes.
items.title: Alexia Barrier finishes fifth as first woman in Ultim class Route du Rhum

items.summary: For the past ten years, Bryde's whales have been returning to Weizhou Island in southern China to feed and breed. Chen Mo and his research team have tracked these giant marine mammals since they were first spotted there, studying their behavior. Their presence has drawn attention to how it may transform local people's attitudes toward nature and marine conservation.
items.title: China's Weizhou Island Becomes Haven for Bryde's Whales

items.summary: Schools in Italy, Scotland and Northern Ireland received bomb threats amid a suspected hoax. In Italy one email reached about 6,300 of 7,476 state schools; some buildings were evacuated as precaution but Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said checks showed no concrete danger. Police Scotland assessed the warnings immediately as hoaxes with no requirement to evacuate. Officials described the incidents as a coordinated cyber-attack rather than genuine risk.
items.title: Bomb Hoax Threatens Schools Across Italy and Scotland

items.summary: Australia's batting coach Graeme Hick called allegations of ball tampering in Usman Khawaja's new book "absolutely false." David Warner, Khawaja's former opening partner, responded on social media and said the tampering was more widely known than just banned trio Warner, Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft. The exchange follows a 2018 South Africa tour.
items.title: Batting coach dismisses Khawaja ball-tampering claims as false

items.summary: Quantum DC chief executive Alby Tomassi said the company has paused plans for a 1200-megawatt hyperscale data centre in Tungkillo, about 41 kilometres east of the Adelaide CBD. The firm would not seek development approval this year but instead run a longer-term engagement programme and convene an independent expert panel to review specialist studies.
items.title: Developer Pauses Adelaide Hills AI Data Centre After Community Pushback

items.summary: France marked the 108th anniversary of the 1918 armistice on Wednesday, with ceremonies carrying distinct political messages ahead of the presidential election. Emmanuel Macron presided over the national ceremony at the Arc de Triomphe in Paris, his last as head of state; it was unpolitical and he did not speak. Marine Le Pen commemorated the day in Hénin-Beaumont, Pas-de-Calais, stressing collective memory, sovereignty and national belonging. Jean-Luc Mélenchon chose Gentioux-Pigerolles, a pacifist monument inscribed "Cursed be war," rejecting conflict preparation with his message "Down with war!" echoing statements on Ukraine.
items.title: French Leaders Mark Armistice Day With Diverging Messages

items.summary: A CGTN commentary titled 'Where green power takes root' describes how renewable energy is transforming rural China, according to the column. Wind turbines across grasslands and deserts provide villages with new dividend income, while solar panels convert rooftops and unused land into assets. Integrated agricultural industries attract young people back home. Green electricity reduces factory costs, supporting village dividends, elderly subsidies and public welfare projects. The piece frames this as China's energy transition playing out on the ground.
items.title: China's Rural Communities Gain Income Through Green Energy Expansion

items.summary: Tens of thousands marched across Spain on Wednesday during a general strike over housing affordability and purchasing power, just weeks before an early election. Unions reported significant turnout in some sectors in the first nationwide 24-hour stoppage since 2012, though business leaders downplayed participation. In central Madrid, demonstrators braved heavy rain carrying house-shaped placards while chanting 'We have no home.'
items.title: Housing Strike Draws Tens of Thousands in Spain

items.summary: Tens of thousands of Polish nationalist sympathisers gathered in Warsaw Wednesday for the annual Independence Day March, days after a deadly shooting spree in Krakow. The event commemorates 1918's end of 123 years of partition by Russia, Prussia and Austria, drawing conservatives through far-right groups.
items.title: Tens of thousands attend Polish nationalist march days after shootings

items.summary: At the COP31 Ministers' Dinner in Antalya on 12 November 2026, Türkiye's environment minister Murat Kurum urged global cooperation against climate change. He said no country could shield itself from rising seas, droughts and extreme weather alone, adding that destinies are interconnected. The conference opened Monday with 196 parties plus the EU.
items.title: Türkiye's COP31 President Calls for Global Climate Cooperation

items.summary: At the COP31 World Leaders Summit in Antalya on Wednesday, London Mayor Sadiq Khan called for accelerated global climate action, warning that delay is not an option. Pointing to severe heat in London, he emphasized early warning systems and pledged, as C40 co-chair representing nearly 1 billion people, to ensure all member cities have them by the end of 2027.
items.title: London Mayor Urges Faster Climate Action at COP31

items.summary: The International Energy Agency says renewable energy expansion over the past 15 years helped India save more than $100 billion in coal and gas import costs. The report projects cumulative savings could reach $240 billion by 2030, with annual savings around $35 billion, assuming fuel prices stay near their 2024-25 average. IEA executive director Fatih Birol said India's experience shows how consistent policies can drive down renewable energy costs and attract investment.
items.title: IEA Credits India's Green Energy Push With $100bn Coal and Gas Savings

items.summary: US officials concluded Alice Huang was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security and allegedly helped move around 240,000 banned Nvidia chips into China. A web of her linked firms is estimated to have secured about $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia AI hardware over three years; Megaspeed alone saw about $4.6 billion through it between 2023 and 2025. Huang admitted an affair with Jensen Huang, now 63, who apologized in a memo as the board opens an independent probe. China rejected the espionage allegations, and Alice Huang has not responded to requests for comment.
items.title: Nvidia CEO's China ties and espionage probe

items.summary: Investor Michael Burry sees a near-term trading opportunity in Nvidia but doubts the controversy surrounding CEO Jensen Huang will damage its business much. In an interview, he said: 'Still, I believe Nvidia's competitive advantage will shrink over the next five years.' The affair admission by Huang has triggered a sharp selloff, wiping out around $430 billion from Nvidia's market value in two sessions. Burry had been shorting Nvidia until September when he exited some put options, though he clarified it was not intended as a bullish signal. He remains concerned about an AI-driven market crash, warning of conditions resembling 1987 and the Dotcom bubble.
items.title: Michael Burry dismisses Nvidia fears amid Huang scandal selloff

items.summary: An alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (Huang Le), may have gained access to Nvidia’s product information and CEO Jensen Huang’s views on Trump AI policy through private conversations with him, The New York Post reported citing an expert. US officials accuse her of links to China's Ministry of State Security, but the allegations remain unproven and Beijing rejects them as groundless. Eftimiades suggested her background could have helped her get close to Huang. Nvidia lost around $430 billion in market value over two sessions amid scrutiny. The company opened an independent investigation into its CEO after he acknowledged being unfaithful, while the FBI examines whether Huang was targeted.
items.title: Nvidia Probe Deepens Over Alleged Chinese Spy and Jensen Huang Affair

items.summary: Nvidia's board appointed former Manhattan federal prosecutor Joon H Kim of Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to investigate whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted in a Chinese intelligence operation amid his extramarital relationship with Alice Huang. Kim will examine information about the couple and allegations that chips were shipped to China.
items.title: Nvidia appoints Joon H Kim to probe Jensen Huang affair and China ties

items.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that a foreign divorce granted on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage does not dissolve the marriage under Indian law, so remarrying can expose a man to bigamy prosecution. The bench held Section 13 of the CPC was violated and rejected the husband’s claim that his British citizenship exempted him from Section 494 of the IPC proceedings opposed by the wife; it quashed cases against the parents and second wife.
items.title: Supreme Court rejects foreign divorce as basis for Indian remarriage

items.summary: CoreWeave shares rose over 26% after strong earnings, lifting battered neocloud stocks including Nebius and Iren. Analysts said CoreWeave’s results eased fears that debt-funded expansion could backfire if demand weakens. Bernstein analysts led by Madison Rezaei called it a best quarter possible but warned CoreWeave may be among the first hit once AI capacity shortages ease, while SoftBank posted a $3.7 billion write-down and Nvidia fell amid Jensen Huang controversy.
items.title: CoreWeave Stock Surge Lifts AI Cloud Peers Amid Nvidia Turmoil

items.summary: HCLTech today launched a pre-configured semiconductor Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) solution built on the PTC Windchill PLM platform to help organizations streamline product development, strengthen quality and compliance and reduce operational complexity. The solution establishes a unified digital thread by connecting people, processes and data across the semiconductor lifecycle, from IP management, new product introduction and supplier collaboration to quality and regulatory compliance.
items.title: HCLTech and PTC Launch Semiconductor PLM Solution Together

items.summary: The India-UK trade pact faces its first major dispute as customs investigators seek a 150% tariff on bulk Scotch whisky shipments from Pernod Ricard and Diageo. The companies sought reduced 75% duty for finished products, but a November 4 memo reportedly instructed officials to apply the higher rate to concentrates classified as compound alcoholic preparations. Dozens of containers are held at ports, with delays threatening supplies.
items.title: India-UK FTA Tariff Dispute Stalls Scotch Whisky Shipments

items.summary: US President Donald Trump defended his administration's military campaign against Iran at the 2026 National Veterans Day Ceremony, asserting that America did not start a war with Iran and that Tehran had been waging war since 1979. He said Washington wanted total victory rather than a partial outcome. The conflict has claimed 23 US service members.
items.title: 'America did not start this': Trump defends war with Iran
